findings.issue: scripts\verify-steps.lock.json is regenerated by scripts:sync whenever a node registers a verify step (A02, A05, A07, A08, A09, A13 and others do), but the owned-path tolerance covers only root package.json and .gitignore. Every registering node therefore fails the owned-path check on a file in A01's scripts\ folder. Also, two parallel nodes that both register will conflict at rebase on root package.json, the .gitignore generated block and verify-steps.lock.json. The spec treats any rebase conflict outside the lockfile as an owned-path defect that escalates.
findings.fix: Add scripts\verify-steps.lock.json to the sync-regenerated tolerance. It is tolerated only when a fresh scripts:sync reproduces all three generated targets byte for byte. At rebase, resolve conflicts in the three generated targets the same way as the lockfile: take main's version, re-run scripts:sync and npm install on the rebased tree, then re-verify. Add a challenge in which T1 and T2 both register a root script in parallel and both reach main without escalation.

findings.issue: The spec does not fix how ESLint finds its config, yet A02, A05 and A09 each ship a nested eslint.config.js. Under the 'majors are floors' rule the builder takes the newest stable ESLint, which is 10.x on the registry today. ESLint 10 looks up the config from each file's own folder by default. A nested config then replaces the root config for its subtree, and module-boundaries, no-float-money and no-weakening-disables silently stop applying in packages/domain, packages/ui and services/api. Under ESLint 9, `eslint .` ignores those nested configs. Either way step 5 can be green while A01's rules do not run.
findings.fix: State the lookup model explicitly. Under ESLint 10 or later, every nested eslint.config.* must spread the root config, exported from scripts\eslint-rules\index.js. A step-4 config check runs `eslint --print-config` on one source file per workspace and fails unless module-boundaries, no-float-money, no-weakening-disables, no-floating-promises and no-explicit-any are all at 'error'. Alternatively, fix ESLint at major 9 with that reason and forbid nested configs in step 4. Add a fault patch: a nested config in a throwaway workspace that omits the root rules must fail verify.

findings.issue: Verify has no code-generation phase before typecheck and lint. Registered steps, including group 'build', run only at step 11, after tsc (step 3) and type-checked ESLint (step 5). A07's and A24's TypeScript imports contracts/typechain-types. A07 says A01 gitignores it, but A01's .gitignore lists only contracts/artifacts and contracts/cache. A09 generates packages/sdk/src/generated at step 11. In a clean clone steps 3 and 5 therefore fail, or the generated typings get committed. The gate re-verify runs in the node's own worktree, not a fresh checkout. Leftover ignored output (a nested .gitignore, .git/info/exclude) hides the problem until the next node's clean run fails, and the failure is blamed on that node.
findings.fix: Add a 'generate' registration group whose steps run between step 2 and step 3, in workspace dependency order. Generated output must be gitignored inside the owning workspace and rebuilt by its generate step. Add contracts/typechain-types/ to A01's static .gitignore, since A07 relies on it. Run the gate verify in a fresh detached checkout of the candidate commit after `npm ci`. Add a challenge: a throwaway workspace whose source imports a gitignored generated file passes a clean-clone verify only through its generate step.

findings.issue: A01 declares `e2e` as a single npm workspace, but no node in final-graph.json owns the e2e\ root files (package.json, tsconfig.json, playwright.config.ts). Fourteen nodes own e2e\<x>\ subfolders: A49, A61, A65, A78-A84, A87, A88, A94, A100 and A103. The first of them must either create e2e\package.json outside its owned paths, which fails the owned-path check, or leave its tests in no workspace, which escapes typecheck (step 3) and the unit-test step (step 7).
findings.fix: Change the workspace glob to `e2e/*`, so each e2e\<x>\ folder is its own workspace owned by its node, and add a shared Playwright base config under scripts\. Alternatively, have A01 own the e2e\ root files (package.json, tsconfig.json, playwright.base.ts), listed in its owned paths and in the graph.

findings.issue: The scope of `eslint .` and `prettier --check .` is undefined, and A01 owns no ignore file. A00's generator writes docs\charter\*.md, the charter *.json files and evidence\A00.json. A01 may never edit them, and they are unlikely to be Prettier-formatted, so A01's own step 6 fails. A07's vendored T-REX submodule (contracts/vendor) would be linted with type-checked rules and format-checked. ESLint flat config does not read .gitignore, so ignored build output (.next, artifacts, .vendor-work) gets linted. A root .prettierignore is not in A01's owned paths, and the registration block has no key for lint or format exclusions.
findings.fix: Specify the scope. ESLint imports .gitignore (includeIgnoreFile) plus a fixed ignore list. Prettier runs with `--ignore-path .gitignore --ignore-path scripts/prettierignore`, a file inside A01's owned paths. Exclude docs\charter\ and machine-written evidence JSON from Prettier. Add a `realx.lintIgnore` registration key limited to the registering workspace's folder, for tracked vendored code such as contracts/vendor/. Add a pass criterion: verify is green on A00's unmodified charter files.

findings.issue: The paragraph 'Nodes that start before the repository exists' assumes A50 and A51 unlock from A00 alone. In final-graph.json they depend on A05 and A00, and A05 depends on A01, so neither can run before A01's commit. The premise copies A00's gate text, which contradicts the graph. It introduces `--exclude-inflight`, which lets any caller hide untracked out-of-path files from the owned-path check, and the spec does not say who may supply the list.
findings.fix: Remove the pre-repository case and the --exclude-inflight flag. If the flag stays, restrict it to A01's own gate, with Fable deriving the list from graph nodes whose status is building. Flag A00's 'Pass unlocks A01, A50 and A51' as inconsistent with the graph.

findings.issue: Step 3 typechecks only 'every workspace with a tsconfig', and the config lint only checks that existing tsconfigs extend the base. A workspace with no tsconfig, or with an include/exclude that leaves source files out, escapes typecheck entirely. Vitest still runs its tests green because it compiles with esbuild and does not typecheck.
findings.fix: In step 4, require every workspace that contains .ts or .tsx files to have a tsconfig that extends the base. Use `tsc --listFilesOnly` to assert that every tracked .ts or .tsx file, excluding declared generated folders, is in the program. Add fault patches for a workspace with no tsconfig and one that excludes src/.

findings.issue: verify:charter checks A00's charter against the live vault graph, which is mutable plan state; A49 already records a pending graph change. Any graph edit that A00's frozen matrix does not reflect turns step 10 red for every in-flight node, and only A00 may fix docs\charter\. Nodes that did nothing wrong get blamed, and verify cannot be reproduced from the commit alone.
findings.fix: The orchestrator pins a snapshot of app-graph.json per milestone, outside the repo, and passes it through REALX_APP_GRAPH. Record its SHA-256 in each node's evidence manifest. A mismatch between charter and graph is classed as a plan defect routed to an A00 respec, not as a node finding.

findings.issue: The evidence pass criterion requires evidence\A01.json to list 'the fault-injection results'. The builder writes that file and never sees Fable's hidden patches; by convention the .json belongs to the builder and the .qa.md to Fable. If the results are recorded with their hidden-patch paths, committed evidence contains gauntlet\hidden\A01\... paths. Evidence is not on the hygiene exemption list, so A01's own hygiene step fails.
findings.fix: Record the fault-injection results in evidence\A01.qa.md (written by Fable), referenced only by case id and hiddenCasesHash. Add a rule that evidence files never carry gauntlet paths, and add that case to the hygiene fault patches.

findings.issue: The secrets scan, the CRLF check (`git ls-files --eol`) and the hygiene check cover only tracked and staged files. Builders make no commits, so every file a node creates stays untracked through its build and fix loops, and these checks see none of it until the orchestrator commits after the gate. A green verify for the builder can differ from a green verify at the gate.
findings.fix: Scan `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` and check the working-tree line endings of untracked files. Keep the pre-commit hook on staged content.

findings.issue: A challenge relies on a 'git log check' to expose a builder that commits mid-build, but no script or verify step defines that check.
findings.fix: Define it in check-owned-paths or as a gate step: in a node worktree, `git rev-list main..HEAD` must be empty before the orchestrator's commit. Add a matching fault patch.

findings.issue: Two interfaces with A00 are not pinned. A00's spec gives check_charter.py no --graph argument, and A01 only lists this as an escalation. The JSON field in agent-access.json that holds the token prefixes is not named; A00 states the prefixes in prose inside its token rules.
findings.fix: Name the JSON pointer for the token prefixes (for example /tokenRules/prefixes), and make the scanner fail loudly if it is missing or empty. Record in A00's spec that check_charter.py accepts --graph and REALX_APP_GRAPH.

findings.issue: The note and the graph have drifted apart. The note estimates 5-7 agent-hours; final-graph.json has est_lo 4 and est_hi 6. The note's owned paths add evidence\A01*, which the graph lacks. The `--json` rule allows output inside evidence\<id>\ 'for the node being verified' but does not say how verify learns the node id.
findings.fix: Align the estimate with the graph, or update the graph and regenerate. Reconcile the evidence owned-path line with the graph. Add a required `--node <id>` argument to verify and refuse any other evidence folder.
